notRecreated.reason: “Boing Boom Tschak” is built from treated voices saying the words, not a synth part. No transcription or MIDI of it was found on Songsterr or BitMIDI.
No transcription or MIDI of “Europe Endless” was found on Songsterr or BitMIDI, so there is nothing to start the chords from.
No transcription or MIDI of “Metropolis” was found on Songsterr or BitMIDI.
The only transcription of “Neon Lights” (Songsterr, Aro Mosley, 2025) has bass and drums, not the string-synth chords this sound is for.
No transcription or MIDI of “Radioland” was found on Songsterr or BitMIDI.
No transcription or MIDI of “Showroom Dummies” was found on Songsterr or BitMIDI.
The part this sound is for is the vocoder’s speech on “Computer World”, which has no notes to transcribe. No transcription of it was found.
The breathing on “Tour de France” is the band’s own breath, recorded, not a synth part, and no lead writes it down.

The “Pocket Calculator” MIDI on BitMIDI (kraftwerk-pocket_calculator.mid) holds the vocal melody, four-note chord stabs and the bass. None is a single-note bleep part: the vocal melody is never taken, and a mono synth cannot play the stabs.
As for the Pro-1’s bleeps: the “Pocket Calculator” lead holds the vocal melody (never taken), four-note stabs (more voices than this sound plays) and the bass.
No transcription or MIDI of “Any Second Now (Voices)” was found on Songsterr or BitMIDI.
The metal percussion on Construction Time Again was sampled metal, and no transcription of a metal-percussion part from the album was found.
Its credit names no work (“early-80s metal percussion”), and no transcription of a metal-percussion part was found.
